skill.name: analysis-tshark
skill.description: Guides authorized TShark packet capture and pcap analysis for security investigations, forensic review, and network troubleshooting.
skill.summary: Analyze packet captures and live traffic with TShark for authorized security investigations.
skill.author: AgentSecOps

security_audit.summary: Most static findings in templates and reference documents are false positives from Markdown, examples, or defensive guidance. Confirmed risks remain in the CI curl-to-bash installer, privileged live packet capture, credential extraction workflows, and TLS key material handling. No prompt injection attempt was found in the reviewed static-analysis files.

remediation.issue: Remote script is piped directly to bash in the CI template.
remediation.suggestion: Replace the curl-to-bash installer with a pinned action, pinned package version, or checksum-verified download before execution.

remediation.issue: The skill presents many sudo packet capture commands as normal workflow steps.
remediation.suggestion: Add explicit confirmation gates, prefer offline pcap analysis first, and document least-privilege capture setup with rollback steps.

remediation.issue: Credential, hash, POST body, and TLS key material extraction can expose secrets.
remediation.suggestion: Move these steps behind an authorized incident-response warning and require redaction, encryption, retention, and access-control guidance in each workflow.

remediation.issue: Troubleshooting guidance grants persistent packet capture capabilities with setcap and group membership changes.
remediation.suggestion: Explain the security impact, limit the recommendation to approved hosts, and include commands or steps to remove the granted capability.

semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited sections are titled Credential Extraction and Credential Harvesting Detection and list specific filters for credentials and hashes. The authorization language reduces malicious intent but not the sensitivity of the capability.

semantic_findings.title: Privileged Live Packet Capture Capability
semantic_findings.description: The skill guides live packet capture on network interfaces and warns that captured traffic may expose sensitive information. This can enable unauthorized monitoring if scope and consent are not enforced.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The file clearly describes packet capture, sensitive information exposure, and live capture commands. The skill includes authorization checks, so this is a controlled dual-use risk rather than overt malicious intent.

content.value_statement: Packet captures can hide incidents, exposed credentials, and abnormal traffic patterns. This skill guides authorized TShark capture, filtering, extraction, and reporting workflows.
actual_capabilities: Explains TShark commands for live capture and offline pcap review.
Provides display filters for HTTP, DNS, TLS, SMB, wireless, and beaconing analysis.
Shows how to export packet fields, files, conversations, and SIEM-ready records.
Covers credential, artifact, and indicator extraction from authorized captures.
Includes operational guidance for retention, redaction, chain of custody, and storage.
limitations: Requires TShark, Wireshark permissions, and access to the relevant interface or capture file.
Live capture can collect private data and must stay within a written authorization scope.
TLS decryption needs approved key material and may not work with modern forward secrecy.
The skill provides guidance only and does not replace legal, privacy, or incident command review.

use_cases.title: Investigate an Active Incident
use_cases.description: Capture short, scoped traffic windows and extract indicators for triage and containment.

use_cases.title: Review a Forensic Packet Capture
use_cases.description: Filter a pcap for protocols, credentials, payloads, and timelines during post-incident analysis.

use_cases.title: Validate Network Controls
use_cases.description: Check whether encryption, segmentation, and monitoring controls expose sensitive traffic.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect a Capture File
prompt_templates.prompt: Use analysis-tshark to inspect this pcap. Summarize protocols, top conversations, DNS names, HTTP hosts, and any obvious sensitive data.

prompt_templates.title: Build Safe Capture Commands
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a short TShark capture plan for an authorized incident window. Include filters, duration, output naming, and data handling steps.

prompt_templates.title: Extract Incident Indicators
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this capture for beaconing, suspicious DNS, executable downloads, unusual POST traffic, and candidate IOCs. Explain each filter.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Forensic Findings
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a repeatable TShark workflow for chain-of-custody analysis. Include artifact extraction, redaction, validation, and a concise findings report.

output_examples.input: A pcap from a suspected workstation compromise.
output_examples.output: A protocol summary, top conversations, DNS and HTTP indicators, suspicious transfer notes, and recommended next triage steps.

output_examples.input: A request to capture traffic during a five minute incident window.
output_examples.output: A scoped capture plan with interface checks, capture filters, duration limits, storage controls, and cleanup guidance.

output_examples.input: A need to find cleartext credentials in legacy protocol traffic.
output_examples.output: A controlled review plan that lists protocol filters, handling rules for secrets, and redaction requirements for reports.

best_practices: Confirm written authorization, scope, retention, and privacy requirements before any live packet capture.
Start with offline pcap analysis when possible, and limit live captures by filter, duration, and packet size.
Encrypt capture files, restrict access, redact sensitive fields, and document chain of custody.
anti_patterns: Capturing broad production traffic without a defined incident scope or retention plan.
Storing extracted credentials, TLS keys, or packet payloads in shared or unencrypted locations.
Running privileged capture commands from unreviewed prompts or on networks you do not administer.

faq.question: Does this skill require TShark to be installed?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill explains TShark workflows and assumes the local environment has TShark or Wireshark tools available.

faq.question: Can it analyze existing capture files?
faq.answer: Yes. Many workflows use offline pcap files and do not require live packet capture.

faq.question: Can it capture live network traffic?
faq.answer: Yes, but only with explicit authorization and proper handling controls. Live capture can expose private data.

faq.question: Does it decrypt TLS traffic automatically?
faq.answer: No. TLS decryption requires approved key material, compatible sessions, and careful protection of any key files.

faq.question: Is this skill suitable for offensive work?
faq.answer: It is dual-use. Marketplace users should apply it only for authorized security operations, forensics, and compliance work.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, or Claude Code use this skill?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.
